brief: Goldman equity sales daily. August payrolls printed +162k against roughly +53k expected with unemployment unchanged at 4.1%, which Privorotsky reads as net firmer, so front-end yields rose while the long end held and pressure shifts onto Friday's CPI, now binary: a benign print lets the Fed wait, a hot core print probably solidifies a hike. September hike odds are back near 60% and 60bps is priced to year end, possibly 75, but strong nominal growth leaves him expecting equity to stay resilient. Oil is the bigger macro problem: Brent near $97, Hormuz tanker traffic at its lowest since May, SPR down to roughly 287m barrels, Iran threatening a formal restricted zone. Because both sides' incentives peak now, his gut sees scope for a diplomatic headline, though evidence of progress is thin. Astra's token efficiency and capability jump imply better cost per task, more usage and more infrastructure spend, so he is not bearish on tech. AfD took 43.8% in Saxony-Anhalt, above 40-41% polling, but France's budget and OATs matter more. Micro improving against harder macro plus light positioning is his wall of worry set-up.
